violation_type.title: Prohibited Punishments - Restrictive device for time out (26 TAC §746.2805(8))
violation_type.short_title: Prohibited Punishments - Restrictive device for time out
violation_type.typical_finding: A 18 mo old was observed to be sitting in a highchair upon arrival. A volunteer was observed removing the child from the chair and telling them they could not hit and not to hit again. The caregiver of the gorup initally stated the chair is only used for eating. After being informed of the volunteer's statement, the caregiver then stated it is used but for only 1 minute.

finding_variants.text: A 18 mo old was observed to be sitting in a highchair upon arrival. A volunteer was observed removing the child from the chair and telling them they could not hit and not to hit again. The caregiver of the gorup initally stated the chair is only used for eating. After being informed of the volunteer's statement, the caregiver then stated it is used but for only 1 minute.
In the Eighteen months classroom, I observed an eighteen month old child sitting in a high chair to prevent disruption during story time.
It was found that a 4 year old in the infant area was placed in a high chair for time out. This was corrected when the 4 year old was taken out of the high chair.

During the inspection 2 children were observed placed in a restrictive device for disciplinary purposes.  This was corrected during the inspection when the caregiver removed the 2 children from the restrictive devices.

During the inspection a child was observed sitting in a high chair while playing on a tablet. When a caregiver was asked why the child was in the highchair it was stated because the child was special needs and would not stop running around.     Note: It was discussed that no child can be confined to any type of restrictive device as a for of discipline.
Based on evidence obtained during the investigation, children under two years of age were placed in restrictive devices for time out.
